semantic_findings.finding: The source has right, left and U-turn prohibitions for bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter, plus a dismount and pedestrian-rule exception. The current matrix has one U-turn dismount comparison. Other turn and actor alternatives still need independent coverage review.

The fixed left-turn cell supports the existing signal comparison and a proved nine-variant traffic sweep, but has no distinct general-zone traversal or adjoining-highway destination comparison. Referenced subsections 3 and 4 and authority-zone facts also remain unresolved.

The source permits straight travel, bars both turns and requires yield to lawful vehicles and pedestrians. The current matrix has one lawful-occupancy yield comparison; the travel and turn alternatives still need review.

The exact law includes a pedestrian on or near a road, at or near a transit stop or boarding, and in or near a school zone or marked or unmarked crosswalk. The only current C233871 comparison changes brake response timing for a pedestrian bodily on the road. Distinct near-road, transit, school and crosswalk setting comparisons have no exact prepared cases in the current branch matrix. The completed C233871 package is preserved while compatible source-bound branch allocations are reviewed.

Independent primary/fallback differential audit of 1,276 candidates across 1,691 ready cases found one fallback construction with omitted top-level measurement_plan, termination_rules and static_checks. Its embedded case-plan also omits camera_plan and source_observation_mapping while changing the reference_corner camera pose. The primary and fallback carry the same identity and recording_description, but this exception needs case-specific semantic review before candidate review can be declared complete. The queue dispatcher now checks source-bound candidate receipts, exact construction hashes, and the selected original camera implementation before running the comparison; CPU probes reject mixed camera sites. Direct invocation of the assignment audit remains outside this dispatch guard, so the candidate review and package-level audit gap remain open. The shared dispatch guard now also evaluates the source-hashed camera function and scene to compare effective camera transforms, with a negative CPU probe for changed function behavior despite an unchanged position table. This protection applies through shared queue dispatch; package-local standalone audits remain unchanged.

Thirty-six comparison-level candidate availability or changed-knob records need case-specific isolation review before unreviewed_candidates can be cleared. Static inventory alone does not establish a violation or physical selection.

Case-specific review of C135705 two_sided_visibility_with_fixed_passage: clear-view fallback1 moves the standing body from y [-3.5,-1.5] to [-4.0,-2.0], while the occluded fallback1 preserves the primary standing footprint and changes only occluder lateral positions. Mixed selection would violate this comparison fixed condition. The independent comparison_audit.py explicitly compares standing_body_xy_m and rejects such a mixed pair, so it cannot silently accept a false fixed-footprint comparison. If the clear-view fallback is selected physically, the local operator needs a matching construction for the paired occluded case or must leave this comparison incomplete. This is a case-specific operational limitation, not a software proof of physical success.

C10307 reference fallback case-specific review: the fallback changes the reference_corner Native camera pose from (0,10,6) m / -20° pitch to (0,7,7) m / -25° pitch, while its four selected comparisons declare the same four-camera contract fixed. The independent comparison_audit.py verifies source contexts and saved delivery receipts but does not compare camera pose or candidate selection. Thus a reference fallback combined with primary peers could pass the comparison audit despite a changed fixed camera. Preserve this as an unresolved candidate-isolation defect until the fallback or its comparisons and bound proofs are corrected; do not infer physical or legal acceptance.
